text: Remote Access: Establishing a Shell via WinRM

WinRM (Windows Remote Management) is a Microsoft protocol that allows for remote management of systems over HTTP/HTTPS. Using <highlight>Evil-WinRM</highlight>, we can obtain an interactive PowerShell session if we have valid user credentials or their NTLM hashes.
When we have recovered the cleartext password (e.g., through cracking a hash with John the Ripper), we can log in directly. This provides a full interactive PowerShell environment.

code:
Info: Establishing connection to <TARGET_IP>...
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\enterprise-security\Documents> whoami
vulnnet\enterprise-security

text: In many cases, we might capture an NTLM hash (e.g., from Mimikatz or SecretsDump) but cannot crack it. WinRM allows us to use the <highlight>NTLM hash</highlight> itself for authentication without ever needing the original password.
Note: When using the <highlight>-H</highlight> flag, you only need the NT portion of the hash (the last part of a standard LM:NT string).

code:
Info: Establishing connection to <TARGET_IP>...
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\enterprise-security\Documents> hostname
VULNNET-PROD

title: Evil-WinRM Advanced Features
items: File Transfer: Built-in 'upload' and 'download' commands for easy file movement
Memory Loading: Ability to load PowerShell scripts directly into memory (Bypassing some AVs)
Persistent Shell: Provides a more stable connection than basic Netcat reverse shells
Pass-the-Hash: Support for NTLM hash authentication for uncrackable passwords
